chapter: Civil service, Keyhole club and civil rights
title: Sorting out Albert's civil service and Keyhole dates
summary: Interviewer untangles when he left civil service, went to New Orleans (1948, a year in the post office) and returned to San Antonio in 1950 to open the new Keyhole.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I'm having a hard time straightening that all out now. Civil service first, then you quit in 40, late 40, then 43 you quit, then 40 opened up the keyhole. Now when did you go back to New Orleans?

No, when I went to New Orleans in 45, 48. 48. And I stayed there for one year, in the post office. And then I came back to San Antonio in 50, to open this other keyhole, this new keyhole, that's on Poplar Street.
